name: Amitriptyline
rationale: High anticholinergic burden; increased risk of falls, delirium, and cognitive impairment in older adults.

name: Diphenhydramine
rationale: Highly anticholinergic; increased risk of confusion, sedation, and falls.
recommendation: Avoid as a sleep aid in older adults ≥65.

name: Diazepam
rationale: Increased sensitivity to benzodiazepines; cognitive impairment, delirium, falls, fractures.
recommendation: Avoid in older adults ≥65 unless safer alternatives have failed.

name: Meperidine
rationale: Normeperidine accumulation causes neurotoxicity; safer alternatives available.

name: Naproxen
rationale: GI bleeding/peptic ulcer risk; increased risk of AKI and fluid retention in older adults.
recommendation: Avoid chronic use unless alternatives are inadequate; if used, add PPI prophylaxis.

name: Indomethacin
rationale: Highest CNS adverse effect risk of all NSAIDs; GI bleeding.

name: Chlordiazepoxide
rationale: Long half-life; increased fall and fracture risk in older adults.

name: Nitrofurantoin
rationale: Pulmonary toxicity and hepatotoxicity with long-term use; inadequate renal clearance at CrCl <30.
recommendation: Avoid for long-term suppression or when CrCl <30 mL/min.

name: Haloperidol
rationale: Increased mortality in patients with dementia-related psychosis.
recommendation: Avoid for dementia-related behavioural problems unless non-pharmacological options have failed.

name: Nifedipine
rationale: Potential for hypotension and myocardial ischaemia; short-acting form.
recommendation: Avoid short-acting nifedipine in older adults ≥65.
